# Sawa Wallet

> Sawa Wallet is a human-first, non-custodial, multi-chain crypto wallet built for Africa and emerging markets. It lets anyone send and receive crypto using just a phone number — no long wallet addresses — and buy, cash out, and spend crypto in local currency.

Sawa Wallet replaces complex wallet addresses with phone numbers, so sending crypto feels as simple as sending a text message. Users own their own keys (non-custodial). It is available on iOS and Android, currently in beta across 50+ countries.

## What Sawa Wallet does

- **Send by phone number**: Send crypto to anyone using their phone number from your contacts — no addresses to copy. Usernames and email work too.
- **Multi-chain, including Bitcoin**: Hold and send USDC, USDT, SOL, ETH, SUI and BTC across Solana, Ethereum, Base, Polygon, BNB Chain, Arbitrum, Optimism and Sui from one wallet.
- **Buy crypto instantly**: Top up with a local bank transfer; crypto arrives in minutes.
- **Cash out locally**: Withdraw to a bank account or mobile money in your local currency.
- **Private rails**: Sawa operates its own on- and off-ramp infrastructure (not public), so conversions are faster and fairly priced with no third-party middleman.
- **In-app swaps**: Trade tokens at the best available rates on Solana and EVM chains, including cross-chain swaps, without leaving the app.
- **Sawa Pay**: Pay bills, buy airtime and data, and settle electricity and cable TV directly from your crypto balance — plus merchant payment links with QR checkout for getting paid.
- **Virtual cards**: Virtual Visa cards to spend your balance anywhere (rolling out soon, starting with Nigeria and South Africa).
- **Earn & protect**: Built-in staking to grow idle assets, and on-chain escrow for safer deals.
- **Non-custodial & secure**: You own your private keys, protected by biometrics and a server-verified passcode with brute-force lockout. Optional identity verification (KYC) unlocks higher limits.
- **Local-first experience**: 7 languages (English, Nigerian Pidgin, Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa, French, Swahili) and 19 display currencies with live exchange rates.

## Who it is for

People sending money to family, paying suppliers across borders, freelancers receiving international payments, and anyone in emerging markets who wants a simple, low-fee way to use stablecoins and crypto in daily life.

## Coverage

50+ countries, with deep local support in Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, South Africa, Uganda, Tanzania, Zambia and more.

## Key facts

- Category: Non-custodial crypto wallet / cross-border payments / stablecoin wallet
- Platforms: iOS and Android
- Networks: Solana, Ethereum, Base, Polygon, BNB Chain, Arbitrum, Optimism, Sui, Bitcoin
- Assets: USDC, USDT, SOL, ETH, SUI, BTC
- Languages: English, Nigerian Pidgin, Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa, French, Swahili
- Cost: Free to use; small transparent fee on fiat conversions
- Custody: Non-custodial (user holds keys)
- Open Source: Sawa Toolkit (@sawa/phone-resolver + @sawa/compliance-kit) — production-extracted primitives for Solana consumer apps. Supports phone, specialized username, and email (mail/username as easier first options before full phone). Private Rust rails power on/off-ramps. Ideal for Solana Foundation Developer Tooling grants.
